errors: The pointwise inequalities φ_{f+g} ≤ φ_f + φ_g and φ_{fg} ≤ φ_f φ_g are false as written. For the sum: f = 1_{[0,1]}, g = 1_{[1,2]} on R gives φ_{f+g}(1.5) = 1 but φ_f(1.5) + φ_g(1.5) = 0. For the product: f = a·1_A + 1_B, g = 1_A + a·1_B with |A| = |B| = 1, a > 1, gives φ_{fg}(1.5) = a > 1 = φ_f(1.5)φ_g(1.5). The correct statements are φ_{f+g}(s+t) ≤ φ_f(s) + φ_g(t) and φ_{fg}(s+t) ≤ φ_f(s)φ_g(t). The integrated consequences on the next page do hold: Φ_{f+g} ≤ Φ_f + Φ_g (Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya) and Ψ_{fg} ≤ Ψ_f + Ψ_g (multiplicative/Horn-type majorization). But they do not follow from the stated pointwise inequalities.

In (4) the infimum over m(E) ≤ t gives the right-continuous version φ^+(t) = lim_{s↓t} φ(s), and m(E) < t gives the left-continuous φ^-. Example: f = 1_{[0,1]} at t = 1. If the labels in the manuscript are as transcribed, they are swapped (the image is hard to read here).
Minor: φ_f ≤ φ_g needs f ≤ g only a.e. Existence of φ_{f+g} from that of φ_f and φ_g needs a subadditivity argument on level sets, which is not given (it is true).

ideas.what: Spectral measure of a function = image measure f(m); decreasing rearrangement φ_f as generalized inverse of the distribution function; equimeasurability ⇔ same rearrangement
ideas.modern_name: distribution function / decreasing rearrangement f^*, equimeasurability
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955), Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace

ideas.what: Variational formula φ_f(t) = inf_{m(E) ≤ t} ||(1−E) f||_∞
ideas.modern_name: generalized s-numbers μ_t(T) = inf{ ||TE|| : τ(1−E) ≤ t }
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fack–Kosaki (1986), who cite Grothendieck 1955 and Ovchinnikov; Murray–von Neumann-type ideas

ideas.what: Calculus of rearrangements (monotone, homogeneous, power-compatible, sub-additive/multiplicative) and ∫ α(f) = ∫ α(φ_f), N_p(f) = N_p(φ_f)
ideas.modern_name: basic properties of f^*; f^*(s+t) ≤ ... inequalities

deep.surprise_reason: This is a commutative draft of material Grothendieck published in Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955), which is already credited, notably by Fack–Kosaki. The variational formula is nice to see in its 1953 commutative origin. The only notable detail is the incorrect pointwise sub-additivity/multiplicativity, which is not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'pour lesquels la partie du second membre de (3) est ambiguë', referring to formula (3) of the previous page; the image reading '(1)' is uncertain.
'Pour que f soit [?] équivalente' should read 'Pour que f soit spectralement équivalente'.
'alors f et g sont [-...-] équivalentes' should read 'f et g sont spectralement équivalentes'.
Struck-out line before (4) is roughly 'si on identifie un ensemble mesurable E avec sa fonction caractéristique', which makes (1−E) meaningful.
Left margin box 2: roughly 'plus généralement, si α est une fonction croissante sur R^+, φ_{α(f)} = α(φ_f), d'où ∫ α(f) = ∫ α(φ_f)'.
Last line: 'admettant la mesure spectrale μ_φ' (V is a misreading of μ).
